chunks: And with the preceding chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Fadhalah, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman ibn Sayabah, from al-Nu'man, from Abu Ja'far, blessings of Allah be upon him, that he said:

"Whoever inquires after the well-being of others, people will inquire after him. And whoever does not prepare patience for the calamities of time will become helpless. And if you make cutting remarks about people, they will make cutting remarks about you; and even if you leave them alone, they will not leave you."
He said: "Then what should I do?" He (the Imam) said: "Lend them from your honour for the day of your need and poverty."

key_terms.الصبر: patience, steadfast endurance in the face of hardship
key_terms.تفقد: to inquire after someone's well-being, to check on others
key_terms.فاقة: destitution, dire need (referring to the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.قرض: to cut, to make cutting remarks; also to lend

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about dealing with people who backbite?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches about social reciprocity and patience. He explains that caring for others brings reciprocal care, while failing to prepare for life's hardships leads to helplessness. When the questioner asks how to handle people's inevitable backbiting, the Imam gives profound advice: invest your dignity as a loan for the Day of Judgment, when you will truly need the reward. This teaching was delivered in the context of early Shia community life where maintaining social bonds despite interpersonal friction was essential.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 11. And with the preceding chains of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Fadhalah, from Abaan, from Abdul Rahman ibn Sayabah, from al-Nu’man, from: Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, who said:

"He who inquires after the well being and whereabouts of the others, people inquire after him when they miss him! And he who does not prepare himself to face the worldly afflictions with patience, ends up helpless. And if you have a habit of passing abrasive comments against other people, then be ready for their remarks. And even if you left them, they would not leave you!"
He said: "Then what shall I do?" He (i.e. Imam) said: "Keep them away from your honour, and leave it for your Day of Hunger and Want (i.e. leave it for the Day of judgement)."
